title: Kafka Producers and Consumers
description: Learn how to produce and consume messages in Kafka using C# and Node.js clients.

data.text: Kafka producers publish messages to topics, while consumers read them back. Mastering the producer and consumer APIs is the first step to building reliable event-driven systems. Both clients offer rich configuration for batching, compression, acknowledgment semantics, and offset management.

A Kafka producer sends records to a topic. Each record has a key, value, timestamp, and optional headers. Producers are thread-safe and can be reused across your application. They batch records for efficiency and compress payloads before sending them to the broker.

data.text: Consumers pull messages from topics by subscribing to one or more topics. Each consumer in a group reads from a distinct set of partitions. Consumers track their position using offsets, which can be committed automatically or manually.

data.title: Keep Consumers Running
data.text: Consumer instances should run continuously in production. Use process managers or container orchestrators like Kubernetes to restart crashed consumers automatically.

items.question: Should I use auto-commit or manual commit?
items.answer: Manual commit gives you full control and prevents data loss during processing failures. Auto-commit is simpler but can skip messages if a consumer crashes between commits.

items.question: Can I have multiple consumers in the same process?
items.answer: Yes. Both Confluent.Kafka and kafkajs allow multiple consumer instances in one process. Just be aware of thread-safety and offset-commit coordination.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Producers publish records to topics with keys, values, and timestamps.
Consumers subscribe to topics and track progress with offsets.
Confluent.Kafka is the standard .NET client; kafkajs is popular for Node.js.
Manual offset commits provide the strongest delivery guarantees.
data.takeaway: Mastering producers and consumers is the foundation of every Kafka integration.
